title: Grade 10 Social Science — Development (Economics)
description: Economic development, national income, HDI, sectors of economy
subject: social-science

questions.question: Development means different things to different people. For a landless rural labourer, development might mean:
options: More jobs, better wages, and security of livelihood
questions.explanation: Development goals differ by circumstance: a landless labourer needs employment and wages; a tribal family may need forest access; a woman may need safety and equality. Development = meeting people's real needs.

questions.question: Per capita income is:
options: Total income of only the richest 10% of people
Total national income / total population — average income per person
questions.explanation: Per capita income = Total National Income / Total Population. Used by the World Bank to classify countries. Limitation: it doesn't show DISTRIBUTION — a high average can hide extreme inequality.

questions.question: The Human Development Index (HDI) measures development using:
options: Three indicators: health (life expectancy), education (literacy/schooling), and standard of living (income)
questions.explanation: HDI (UNDP) measures: (1) Long and healthy life (life expectancy at birth); (2) Knowledge (mean + expected years of schooling); (3) Decent standard of living (GNI per capita at PPP). Range: 0 to 1.

questions.question: Kerala has a high HDI despite lower per capita income than some other states because:
options: It has high literacy, good healthcare, and social equity — especially for women
It receives more central government funds
Its geography gives it natural advantages
questions.explanation: Kerala invests heavily in education and healthcare. Its literacy rate (~99%) and life expectancy are among India's highest. This shows that development is not just about income — social investment matters.

questions.question: The primary sector of the economy includes:
options: Agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining (extraction from nature)
questions.explanation: Primary sector: activities directly using natural resources — farming, fishing, mining, forestry, animal husbandry. Secondary sector: manufacturing. Tertiary sector: services (banking, trade, transport).

questions.question: Sustainable development means:
options: Maximising present economic growth at any cost
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
questions.explanation: Sustainable Development (Brundtland Commission, 1987): present development must not destroy resources/environment needed by future generations. It balances economic, social, and environmental concerns.

questions.question: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures:
options: Total value of goods and services produced within a country in a year
questions.explanation: GDP = total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given year. GNI (formerly GNP) adds income from abroad. GDP per capita = GDP ÷ population.

questions.question: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is an indicator of development because:
options: More infants born means higher GDP
Low IMR indicates better healthcare, nutrition, and living conditions for all
High IMR means more population growth
questions.explanation: IMR = number of children dying before age 1 per 1000 live births. Low IMR = good healthcare, clean water, nutrition, and maternal care. It's a sensitive measure of overall social development.

questions.question: Punjab has a high per capita income but relatively lower HDI rank compared to Kerala because:
options: Punjab's income growth hasn't equally translated into health/education improvements for all, unlike Kerala's model
Kerala has higher per capita income
questions.explanation: Punjab's per capita income is high (Green Revolution agriculture) but social indicators lag — female literacy, infant mortality in some areas. Kerala prioritised human development spending, achieving better HDI despite lower income.

questions.question: Public Distribution System (PDS) in India is an example of:
options: Government intervention to ensure food security for the poor (subsidised food grains)
questions.explanation: PDS distributes subsidised food grains (rice, wheat) to Below-Poverty-Line households through 'ration shops'. It is a key food security measure, reducing hunger even if per capita income is low.

questions.question: The literacy rate in India's economic context primarily matters because:
options: It allows people to read newspapers
Educated people are more productive, earn better, can access healthcare information, and participate in democracy
The government collects more taxes from educated people
questions.explanation: Literacy is both an end (human development goal) and a means: literate people earn more, manage health better, participate in democracy, and are better able to demand their rights.

questions.question: The body that publishes the Human Development Report annually is:
questions.explanation: The UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) publishes the annual Human Development Report and Human Development Index. It tracks development progress across 191+ countries.

questions.question: Underground (black) economy refers to:
options: Economic activities not reported to the government (untaxed, informal, illegal)
questions.explanation: The underground (informal/black) economy includes unreported economic activity — street vendors, informal labour, black market transactions — not captured in official GDP. It is a challenge for accurate national income measurement.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of 'non-material' aspects of development?
questions.explanation: Development includes non-material aspects: freedom, equality, dignity, political rights, security, and cultural values. GDP growth is a material indicator. True development encompasses both material AND non-material well-being.

questions.question: Net Attendance Ratio in education measures:
options: Number of schools in a district
The percentage of children of school-going age who attend school
questions.explanation: Net Attendance Ratio = (number of children of school-going age attending school / total number of children of that age) × 100. It is a key educational development indicator.
